claim: *Chunked residency versus skeletonized residency.* (a) Page chunking limits how much document state and associated media a worker holds at once, but media remains part of the worker's resident representation. (b) Skeletonization keeps only document structure and media references resident. Individual media objects stream from external storage to the consumer on demand, so total media size no longer determines persistent worker memory.
topology: Side-by-side resident-media workers versus skeleton worker and external streamed media; dashed reference retained.
required_terms: Each chunk still carries its media in the worker.
bw_encoding: Black strokes and text; pale gray headers only. Dashed paths retain optional, missing, or forbidden semantics where explicitly labeled. Position, containment, line weight, and written labels carry distinctions without color.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames.
alt:
Two panels. (a) Chunked, format-native representation: an OOXML document is split into
    page chunks, and each of several workers holds its chunk's structural state together with the media for
    that chunk, so media remains part of the worker's resident representation. (b) Skeletonized
    representation: the OOXML document becomes a structural skeleton plus media references held by the
    worker, while media stays in an external store and individual media objects stream to the GenAI service
    on demand. Total media size no longer determines persistent worker memory.
